TEXT
Money has always fascinated human beings. Some people spend their whole lives running after wealth, convinced that money is the key to happiness. It is true that money is necessary: it provides food, shelter, health care and education. Nobody can be happy in extreme poverty. However, money alone cannot buy the most important things in life. It cannot buy true love, real friendship, good health or peace of mind. History is full of rich people who were deeply unhappy, and of poor people who lived with dignity and joy. The problem begins when money becomes a goal in itself rather than a means. A person who sacrifices everything — family, health, values — for the sake of money often ends up with a full bank account but an empty heart. In the end, the wisest attitude is to use money to live well, not to let money rule our lives.

I. READING COMPREHENSION (8 marks)
1) Why do some people spend their lives running after wealth?   (2 marks)
2) In what way is money "necessary", according to the text?   (2 marks)
3) What important things can money not buy?   (2 marks)
4) What happens to a person who sacrifices everything for money?   (2 marks)

II. LANGUAGE (6 marks)
1) Complete with a relative pronoun (who / which): A person ______ sacrifices everything for money ends up unhappy.   (1,5 marks)
2) "Nobody can be happy in extreme poverty": rewrite starting with "Everybody…".   (2 marks)
3) Give the superlative: Money cannot buy ______ (important) things in life.   (1,5 marks)
4) Give the opposite of "wealth" = ______.   (1 mark)

III. WRITING (6 marks)
"Can money buy happiness?" Write a composition (about 12-14 lines) giving your balanced opinion, with arguments and examples. Use linkers.
